title: Network Error: Address Already in Use (Port Conflict)
symptoms: bind() to 0.0.0.0:80 failed (98: Address already in use)
listen tcp :8080: bind: address already in use
root_cause: Another process is already listening on the requested TCP or UDP port, or an earlier instance of the application is stuck in TIME_WAIT or hanging in the background.
diagnostic_steps: Identify the PID and process holding the port: sudo ss -tulpn | grep :<port_number>
Alternatively check with lsof: sudo lsof -i :<port_number>
remediation_commands: sudo kill -9 <PID>   # Force terminate if hung
# Or reconfigure your application to bind to an alternative port in its config

title: DNS Error: Temporary Failure in Name Resolution / Could Not Resolve Host
root_cause: The system cannot query configured DNS nameservers. This is usually caused by broken /etc/resolv.conf symlinks, systemd-resolved service being stopped, network interfaces missing DNS gateway options, or restrictive outbound firewall rules on UDP port 53.
diagnostic_steps: Check systemd-resolved status: resolvectl status || systemd-resolve --status
Test direct DNS query to public DNS: dig @8.8.8.8 google.com || nslookup google.com 1.1.1.1
Test ping to an IP address directly to verify network connectivity: ping -c 3 8.8.8.8
remediation_commands: # If /etc/resolv.conf is broken or empty, configure a reliable fallback nameserver:

title: Network Error: Connection Refused (ECONNREFUSED)
symptoms: curl: (7) Failed to connect to host port: Connection refused
root_cause: The client reached the host IP, but no application is listening on that port, or the application is bound strictly to localhost (127.0.0.1) and rejecting external connections.
diagnostic_steps: Verify the service is actually running: sudo systemctl status <service>
Check what IP address the service is listening on: sudo ss -tulpn | grep :<port>
Look for 127.0.0.1 vs 0.0.0.0 binding (localhost only vs all interfaces)
Check local firewall: sudo ufw status || sudo iptables -L -n -v
remediation_commands: # Change bind address from 127.0.0.1 to 0.0.0.0 in the application configuration if external access is needed
